T890 (can a dispatcher still be handed a serving tag that cannot serve?) — answered NO, refused by name. Advances L1 (the dashboard tells the truth).

DEFECT: bin/subagent --provider ollama --model kimi-k2.7:cloud was accepted (both kimi-k2.7:cloud and kimi-k2.7-code:cloud canonicalize to kimi-k2.7), launched, and died in 0.9 s — reported to the operator as a nonce failure ('the worker did not read the bundle') when the model was never reached. bin/dispatch was immune (it canonicalizes then RE-DERIVES the live serving tag from its MODELS table). Two paths did the same thing differently; the un-gated one walked into a death the gated one sidesteps. model-registry.md had recorded kimi-k2.7:cloud as do-NOT-dispatch since 2026-08-18 — prose is not a remedy for a mechanism failure.

FIX (bin/subagent only — held by T890; bin/dispatch untouched):
- The serving tag used for launch is ALWAYS re-derived from the canonical label (new CANONICAL_TO_OLLAMA_TAG / CANONICAL_TO_PI_TAG maps, the one source of truth for the LIVE tag); the hand-typed raw tag is never passed through. A load-time assertion + tools/regression-serving-tag-single-path.sh arm 5 verify the live-tag maps <-> the canonicalization maps (OLLAMA_TAG_TO_CANONICAL/PI_TAG_TO_CANONICAL, kept for input convenience + the existing regression-ollama-dispatcher.sh control 6) <-> src/managent/main.zig canonical_models[] <-> bin/dispatch MODELS agree — one truth, verified not duplicated.
- arm A (input mismatch): a hand-typed serving tag that does not match the derived LIVE tag is REFUSED by name before any host check — the dead-tag class. The dead alias entry kimi-k2.7:cloud was DELETED from OLLAMA_TAG_TO_CANONICAL (deletion before addition); it canonicalizes via the generic :cloud strip then arm A refuses it.
- arm B (host validation, ollama only): the derived live tag is validated against `ollama list` BEFORE any child is spawned (WEIZIGO_OLLAMA_OFFERED injects the host offering for tests, mirroring WEIZIGO_HOST_MEM_AVAIL_MB); refused by name if absent. If the offering is unknowable (ollama unreachable, env unset) the check is SKIPPED — a real launch surfaces the failure, a dry-run previews.
- RAM declaration fixed too: _declared_ram_mb now receives live_tag (carries :cloud for cloud models), not raw_model — a canonical-label input (kimi-k2.7) previously mis-declared the resident 18 GB figure instead of the cloud 3328 MB figure.
- The T792 gap the old docstring named is closed: an unrecognized tag (e.g. retired kimi-k2-thinking:cloud) is now REFUSED (canonicalizes to a label not in the live-tag map) instead of silently producing a non-canonical label.

SCOPE 3 (launch failure != nonce failure): the dead-tag defect is now refused before launch, so the false-nonce-accusation cannot recur for that class. The BROADER separation ('model never reached' vs 'worker did not follow instructions') belongs in the verifier (tools/dispatch_verify.py), NOT the dispatcher: a worker that produced NO meaningful output (rc!=0, empty/near-empty stdout) is a launch failure, not a nonce failure. RECOMMENDED FOLLOW-UP ROW: a task holding tools/dispatch_verify.py (T709 dispatchable holds it) to distinguish rc!=0 + empty stdout as 'LAUNCH FAILURE / model never reached' from a genuine nonce-missing work failure. Not done here — T890 holds bin/subagent, not dispatch_verify.py.

SCOPE 4 (reconcile the two entry points' gates): bin/dispatch enforces bundle/row gates (title T505, landmark T747, directive T625, row-state, bundle-exactly-one, fleet-cap T845, holds T500); bin/subagent enforces launch gates (depth cap, window cooldown T628/T677, admission T821, and now serving-tag T890). RECOMMENDATION (defended): bin/subagent should remain the public launch chokepoint (managers dispatch sub-rows via it; it cannot refuse T-ids), and the bundle/row gates it lacks should be SHARED with bin/dispatch by extracting them into a common module (one implementation, two callers) rather than duplicated — duplication is the drift this project keeps paying for. Not implemented here (scope: T890 is the serving-tag fix; gate extraction is a refactor touching bin/dispatch, which T890 does not hold). Filed as a follow-up.

PRE-EXISTING TEST-ISOLATION BUG SURFACED (the commit's TEST_GATE_BYPASS reason): the pre-commit hook's fast test tier runs in PARALLEL (TEST_GATE_WORKERS). regression-depth-enforcement.sh and regression-ollama-dispatcher.sh BOTH dispatch 'bin/subagent T996 ...', and bin/subagent's T-id resolution globs 'untracked/T996-*.md' requiring EXACTLY ONE bundle. Each script creates its own T996 bundle (T996-regression-depth.md / T996-regression-ollama-dispatcher.md) and cleans up via an EXIT trap. Run SERIALLY each is fine (one bundle at a time); run in PARALLEL both bundles coexist, the glob finds 2, and every 'subagent T996' call fails 'expected one bundle for T996, found 2' — so depth-enforcement fails ALL its arms and ollama-dispatcher fails too (on top of its ambient control-4). Confirmed IDENTICAL with bin/subagent stashed to HEAD (the collision is in unchanged T-id-glob code, not the T890 fix) — so NOT a T890 regression; both scripts pass serially (depth-enforcement rc=0). My staging bin/subagent caused the hook to SELECT both into the fast tier (they cover bin/subagent), surfacing the collision. FOLLOW-UP ROW (filed): give one of the two scripts a distinct T-id (e.g. T997) so they are parallel-safe — a tooling fix, out of T890's scope (neither script is a T890 hold). Committed with TEST_GATE_BYPASS=<recorded reason> (the hook's documented escape for a pre-existing failure not yet in the S09 known-red baseline).
